01 / The short version

Every room you fill starts with a search.

Families looking for assisted living in Magnolia start on Google, and more and more of them start by asking AI tools like ChatGPT. Your website is where they decide whether to call.

Mr. Daniel,

I went through dunamisplace.com the way a daughter looking for care for her mom would. The good news: the basics are there. Your address is easy to find, your phone number is one tap away on a phone, and your services and amenities are real and specific.

But I found three places where families get stuck. When a family gets stuck, they don't wait. They go back to Google and call the next home on the list. Every one of those is a room that stays empty longer.

  1. Families can't tell if your home is right for their parent.
  2. Your care pages don't say clearly what you offer.
  3. Nobody can be sure your inquiry forms are reaching you.

From what you shared, you've already put real money into websites and still can't tell which one brings families in. That's the bigger problem, and it's the one I'd solve. Not just a new website, but a system that brings families to you and shows you where each one came from.

AIA KINGS · Dunamis Place02
Problem 1 / Families can't tell if you're a fit

The page that answers "Can you care for my mom?" is empty.

Your homepage tells families to check their eligibility. When they click, they find a placeholder.

This is the most important question a family has, and it's the moment they're closest to picking up the phone. Instead of an answer, they land on a page with nothing on it. A family that can't tell if you're a fit doesn't call to ask. They call a home that already told them.

What it costs you: families who were ready to call, at the exact moment they were ready.

The fix: a clear page, in your words and approved by you, that explains who you care for, how the assessment works, and who to call. Then one obvious button to call or book a tour.

AIA KINGS · Dunamis Place03
Problem 2 / Your care pages are confusing

Families and referrers can't tell what you actually provide.

Two of your care pages mix up services, so it's hard to tell what Dunamis does itself and what comes from outside providers.

Your Adult Day Care page lists hospice, home health, medical equipment, visiting doctors and physical therapy all together, without saying who provides them. Your Alzheimer's and Dementia page repeats the adult day care wording.

That matters most for referrals. Hospital discharge planners, social workers and doctors' offices send families to homes they're sure about. If they can't tell from your site what you do, they send that family somewhere they can.

What it costs you: referrals, some of the best families you can get, because someone they trust already sent them to you.

The fix: one clear page for each type of care you offer, saying what Dunamis provides, what you coordinate with outside providers, and who it's right for. You approve every word about care.

The official Texas state listing confirms your Magnolia address and your assisted living license, so the foundation is solid. The pages just need to say it clearly.

AIA KINGS · Dunamis Place04
Problem 3 / Nobody knows if inquiries arrive

A family fills out your form. Then what?

There's a warning showing next to your forms, and nobody has checked that messages actually reach you.

Right next to your appointment form, visitors can see a warning from your site's spam protection saying its free limit has run out. I didn't send a test, so I can't tell you the forms are broken. But I can't tell you they work either, and from what you shared, neither can anyone else.

The form also asks for a lot (full street address, ZIP, best time to call) and never says whether sending it books a visit or just asks for one. A family who thinks they booked a tour and never hears back doesn't try twice.

One more thing: your website lists 832-661-8306, and your state listing shows 832-521-3088. Make sure both ring someone.

What it costs you: families who already chose you and tried to reach you. These are the most expensive ones to lose.

The fix: a short form that asks only what you need to call them back, says exactly what happens next, and goes to a named person on your team. Then I'd test it start to finish with you, so you know it works.

05 / Why this is bigger than a website

Your website is property. Right now it's on a side street.

Think of your online presence like real estate. The better the location and the stronger the building, the more people walk in, every month, for years.

  • Your website is the building. It's property you own. Today it's a building with an empty front office and a confusing sign.
  • Google and AI search are the location. When a family searches "assisted living near Magnolia" or asks ChatGPT for a recommendation, that's foot traffic. SEO moves your building onto the busy street. AI SEO makes sure the AI tools families ask can read your facts and recommend you with confidence.
  • Reviews are your reputation on the block. They're why a family picks you over the home down the road.
  • Ads are rent. They work, but the day you stop paying, the traffic stops.

This is why I don't sell websites by themselves. Rent stops paying when you stop paying. Property you own keeps working, and it gains value over time. Every month your site shows up, collects reviews and answers families' questions, it gets harder for a competitor to take that spot from you.

Nobody can promise a specific ranking or a place in an AI answer, and I won't. What I can do is build the property right, put it in the strongest position possible, and keep making it stronger.

Optional / The technical details

For whoever runs your website.

This part gets technical. You don't need it to act on anything above. It's here if you're curious or want to hand it to whoever runs your site.

  • Eligibility page: /assisted-living-home-eligibility-for-senior-care is linked from the homepage and listed in the sitemap, but contains only a holding message.
  • Canonical tags: all 23 pages in the page sitemap load over HTTPS but declare HTTP canonical URLs. Homepage social and schema identifiers also use HTTP. Google treats this as a conflicting signal.
  • robots.txt: disallows /wp-content/, /wp-includes/ and uploads, which blocks crawlers from the CSS, scripts and images used to render the pages.
  • Meta descriptions: all 23 pages reuse one generic description. Titles are unique but target Texas broadly rather than Magnolia.
  • Structured data: Yoast outputs WebSite, WebPage and BreadcrumbList only. No LocalBusiness or Organization markup carrying the address and phone.
  • reCAPTCHA: a reCAPTCHA Enterprise free-quota warning renders beside the appointment, contact and referral forms. No submissions were sent.
  • Forms: same-origin WordPress theme iframes with no title attributes. Where submissions go (email, CRM) needs account access to confirm.
  • Analytics: WP Statistics code is on every page. Whether it collects usable data needs account access.
  • Platform: WordPress (Proweaver footer credit), Yoast, WP Rocket. Some responses expose PHP 7.2.34, and several standard security headers are missing.
  • Speed: Google's public PageSpeed test returned a quota error, so no speed score is reported.

Method: public pages only, reviewed October 16, 2026 at desktop and phone sizes. No forms submitted, no calls placed, no accounts accessed. The full audit is available on request.
